title: Nanoparticle Protein Coronas Differentially Interrogate Proteomes with Superior Performance Compared to Conventional Deep Proteome Workflows
projectDescription: The superior performance of a multiple NP workflow was shown compared to high-complexity, state-of-the-art, high-pH fractionation strategies in terms of depth and precision. We also evaluate the link between the physicochemical properties of NPs and their differential protein selectivity.
sampleProcessingProtocol: We compared a panel of 5 nanoparticles to a high-pH fractionation of plasma depleted for high-abundance proteins (deep fractionation) in which 19 fractions were concatenated to 9 final fractions, depleted plasma (without any fractionation), and neat plasma using 30-min gradients and data-independent acquisition (DIA).
dataProcessingProtocol: The SWATH data was processed using the DIANN analytical software (version 1.8). in library-free mode. The neural network classifier was set to double-pass mode. The rest of the parameters were set to default. The Q-value cutoff at precursor and protein level was set to 0.01. Statistical analysis and visualization were performed using R (v3.5.2) with appropriate packages.
